WHOLE PROMOTION, 8 of 8 functions, destructor pair included. The cartridge orders D1 (0x021118c8) BELOW D0 (0x02111928) -- the reproducible direction. mwccarm 2004/b56's destructor-variant lever set is closed and measured: a destructor defined in the class body emits D1 then D0 and nothing else, while an out-of-line definition emits D2, D0, D1 plus a homeless D2 the ROM does not carry. include/daDkk_c.h was moved to the in-class form for exactly that reason, and tubuild verify reports 8/8 MATCH with all eight sections in ROM-ascending emission order. This is the direction its own base class daDsnBase_c could NOT reproduce -- ov091 orders that one D0-below-D1, which is why daDsnBase_c promoted 9-of-11 while this leaf promotes whole.

The class's vtable, emitted by this TU because it defines the key function (daDkk_c::InitResources -- the first declared virtual that is neither inline nor pure, now that the destructor is defined in the class body). Section size 0x88 = 2 preamble words + 32 slots. The slot count is proven from the cartridge rather than from symbols.txt spacing: config/arm9/overlays/ov025/relocs.txt relocates every word from 0x0211384c (the typeinfo pointer, to _ZTI7daDkk_c at 0x021137ec) through 0x021138cc (slot 31, to ov002:0x020ee55c dBgActor_c::Kill), and the next relocated word 0x021138d0 already belongs to _ZTI14daObjDpBrock_c. The three ambiguous data_ov025_021138a8/021138bc/021138c4 rows fall inside the table and are phantom interior symbols; reading the extent from the next symbols.txt row would give a false 0x58. 32 slots is also what the dBgActor_c length rule predicts and what the base class daDsnBase_c's own vtable carries, since this leaf adds no new virtual. Corroborated from the object side at build time: romdata_check.check_object() compares 128 emitted bytes (32 words) against the retail ov025 image with relocations applied and blindWords 0 -- all 128 equal, verdict VERIFIED. Note that the same record's own romExtent field reads 88 decimal, i.e. the false 0x58 taken from data_ov025_021138a8; the emitted-and-compared 128 is the number that is proven, not that one. The canonical copy is in THIS module at ov025:0x02113850 but outside the licensed range (.text 0x021118c8-0x02111cf4), which is .text only, so dsd supplies it as ROM data.

Vector3's four-byte inline destructor, emitted as vague linkage because this TU odr-uses Vector3 as a local: func_ov025_02111a84 takes a Vector3 v[2] and daDkk_c::InitResources takes four more. No member of daDkk_c has that type -- the trigger is what the TU touches, not what it stores. The cartridge owns the body at arm9:0x020072c0 and an enrolled source already reaches it, so this object's copy is a duplicate that production isolation discards. Unlike the base class daDsnBase_c, this TU emits no _ZN<N>@class$<n>daDkk_c_cppD1Ev companion: that symbol appears only when the source declares a file-local anonymous struct to hold the Vector3 locals, and every local here is a plain object or array.
